Spec quality checklist re-validated: all 16 checkbox items still pass against the updated spec, so no markers changed and the file was left untouched (no noisy diff).

## Extension Hooks

Command: `/speckit-git-commit`
Description: Auto-commit after spec clarification

Prompt: Commit clarification changes?
To execute: `/speckit-git-commit`

---

## Completion Report

**Questions asked & answered**: 5 of 5. You delegated the decision on all five; each recommendation was taken, with the reasoning recorded in the spec.

**Updated spec**: `specs/002-import-html-export/spec.md`

**Decisions recorded**

| # | Decision |
|---|----------|
| 1 | HTML escaping is a **closed** set — `&`, `<`, `>` in address/title/labels, plus `"` in `href` only; `'` stays literal; `&` substituted first; output asserted byte-for-byte |
| 2 | CSV header compared **after parsing**, so `"id","url","title","tags"` is accepted; wrong names/order/count still status 2 |
| 3 | A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is **discarded**, both shapes; invalid UTF-8 is a status-2 file error |
| 4 | A blank line is a zero-field row → **status 2**; the newline ending the last row is not a blank record, so the tool's own export imports cleanly |
| 5 | A successful `imported 0` **creates** an absent store, like every other command; only a *failed* import leaves no file |

**Sections touched**: Clarifications (new), User Story 1 Acceptance Scenarios (7, 9), User Story 2 Acceptance Scenarios (5, new 6, renumbered 7–9), Edge Cases, Functional Requirements (new FR-002a, FR-006, new FR-006a, FR-009, FR-010, FR-014), Success Criteria (SC-003, SC-004), Assumptions.

**Spec Quality Checklist**: 16/16 → 16/16 items passing. No items changed state; none outstanding.

**Coverage summary**

| Category | Status |
|---|---|
| Functional Scope & Behavior | Clear |
| Domain & Data Model | Clear |
| Interaction & UX Flow | Clear |
| Non-Functional Quality Attributes | Clear (SC-005 bounds both operations) |
| Integration & External Dependencies | **Resolved** — file-shape tolerance pinned (header quoting, byte-order mark, blank lines) |
| Edge Cases & Failure Handling | **Resolved** — blank line, invalid UTF-8, zero-count store creation now specified |
| Constraints & Tradeoffs | Clear |
| Terminology & Consistency | **Resolved** — "header line" → "header record" normalised across FR-010, SC-003 and the scenarios |
| Completion Signals | **Resolved** — web-page output is now byte-assertable rather than "at minimum" escaped |
| Misc / Placeholders | Clear — no markers, no unquantified adjectives |

Nothing is Outstanding or Deferred. Two things worth knowing about the result: FR-014 is now stricter than it was, so any implementation using a default HTML-escaping helper that also escapes `'` will fail its test — that is intended, since byte-predictable output was the point. And decisions 2 and 3 deliberately loosen input tolerance for spreadsheet round-trips while decision 4 keeps it strict on blank lines; that split is consistent (a quoted header and a byte-order mark carry no bookmark data and lose nothing, whereas a malformed row might).

**Suggested next command**: `/speckit-plan` — the spec is ready, with the one caveat above for the planner to carry into test design.
